facts.fact: 4.5 names the sequencer's types Strip, ImageStrip, MovieStrip, StripsTopLevel, StripElement; the pre-4.4 Sequence names are gone from bpy.types
a scene made with bpy.data.scenes.new has no sequence editor (None) until sequence_editor_create(); the factory scene already has one
sequence_editor_create() returns the editor; .strips and the deprecated .sequences both exist
strips.new_image(name, filepath, channel, frame_start) makes a 1-frame image strip; elements.append(filename) adds frames from the same directory, and the strip lengthens to match

fit_method is only an argument of new_image/new_movie (no strip property); a 128 x 96 image in a 256 x 192 scene gets transform.scale 1 with ORIGINAL (the default: drawn at its pixel size, a quarter of the frame) and 2 with FIT
the deprecated sequence_editor.sequences still works in 4.5 and warns nothing through Python's warnings
bpy.ops.sequencer.image_strip_add fails its poll in background mode without an override (use strips.new_image)
result: RuntimeError: Operator bpy.ops.sequencer.image_strip_add.poll() failed, context is incorrect

facts.fact: rendering the strips scene writes one MP4 with every frame (12), read back by movieclips.load
strips.new_movie reads the clip's length into frame_final_duration (12 here)
in a scene that has strips, a frame no strip covers renders black, not the 3D view
a scene that has strips renders the strips, not its 3D view (frame 12 rendered as the strip's image, frame 1); with render.use_sequencer = False it renders the 3D scene again
